responseBinding.questionText: Which section describes preventing moisture from distorting later comparisons?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: C Drying and stabilising the sample

rows.sourceExcerpt:
C Drying and stabilising the sample
Fresh cores contain variable moisture, and water strongly affects X-ray attenuation. Comparing wet samples would make density differences difficult to interpret. The cores are therefore dried under controlled conditions until their mass becomes stable. They are then fixed in straight supports so that movement during scanning does not blur the image. This preparation may look routine, yet it creates a common baseline. If one sample retains more moisture or bends inside the scanner, the resulting profile can resemble a genuine biological change even though it was produced by handling.

responseBinding.questionText: Which section explains why ring width does not show every change within a year?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: A From ring width to density

rows.sourceExcerpt:
A From ring width to density
For more than a century, researchers have compared the widths of annual tree rings. Wide rings often indicate favourable growth, while narrow ones may record drought, cold or competition. Width, however, is only one measurement. Wood formed early in a growing season has large, thin-walled cells, whereas late-season wood is commonly denser. A density profile can therefore reveal changes within a single year that a ruler cannot show. Modern laboratories increasingly combine traditional chronology with X-ray computed tomography, or CT, to measure these internal contrasts without cutting a core into many fragile slices.

responseBinding.questionText: Which section describes checking automatic boundaries against neighbouring trees?

F Locating annual boundaries
Density values rise and fall along the corrected path, but the computer does not always know where one year ends. responseBinding.questionText: Which section explains converting scanner intensity into physical estimates?

rows.sourceExcerpt:
D Calibrating the scanner
A CT scanner does not directly print wood density in familiar units. It records how strongly many narrow X-ray beams are weakened as they pass through the sample. Before a batch is analysed, reference materials of known density are scanned with the cores. Their values form a calibration curve that converts image intensity into estimated physical density. Calibration is also why results from two institutions cannot be compared safely merely because both used CT: their reference standards and reconstruction choices must also be compatible.

responseBinding.questionText: Which section warns that environmental association is not proof of cause?

rows.sourceExcerpt:
G Interpreting the archive
Once the sequence is dated, scientists can calculate annual maximum density, minimum density and other features. The values may be related to temperature, rainfall or disturbance, but association is not simple proof. Tree age, competition and species-specific growth can produce similar signals. Large studies therefore combine many trees and retain metadata about sampling and processing. CT expands what can be recovered from a small core and preserves a digital record for reanalysis; it does not remove the need for careful field design, calibration or cautious ecological reasoning. Archived scans also let a later team test a new measurement rule without borrowing or rescanning the physical core. Even then, researchers must preserve the original image settings and calibration record. Otherwise, a refined algorithm may create a more detailed result whose relationship to real density is uncertain.

responseBinding.questionText: The author states that water sounds are preferred by most city residents.

rows.sourceExcerpt:
H Limits and accountability
Definitions should remain transparent. If an authority labels a site quiet solely because its average level falls below a threshold, it may ignore users who find the route inaccessible or threatening. Conversely, satisfaction surveys alone can overlook damaging exposure. A defensible programme publishes both acoustic and experiential criteria, reports when measurements were taken and repeats assessment after changes. There is no universal sound that guarantees wellbeing. The strongest evidence comes from converging measures and from acknowledging whose experience is missing. Long-term stewardship is equally important. A water feature that stops working or planting that blocks sight lines can reverse the qualities recorded in an opening-day survey. Authorities should assign responsibility for maintenance and provide a way for users to report changes. Seasonal audits can then distinguish temporary disturbance from a persistent decline. bindings.audiblePhrase: Neither is necessary because your name will be on my list. Please bring photo ID, though. We must confirm the person receiving the gate code is the applicant.

responseBinding.questionText: What protective item will the allotment provide?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Closed shoes are enough for the induction, and safety glasses aren't needed for the basic tour. We provide gardening gloves, so don't buy those specially. Just choose a pair when you arrive.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The office is closed on induction mornings. Email the volunteer team instead; one of them monitors that inbox from half past eight and can tell you whether the group has entered the site.

responseBinding.questionText: The basic feedstock often includes agricultural ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The starting mixture is usually described as a substrate. Rather than using a solid sheet of finished paper, producers may begin with husks, stalk fragments or similar material left after crops are harvested or processed. In materials research, these secondary agricultural streams are commonly grouped under the term residue. They provide both physical bulk and nutrients, although their exact composition depends on the original crop and on what happened during processing.

responseBinding.questionText: The fine fungal threads are known as ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The fungus is easy to misunderstand because a mushroom is the part most people recognise. Inside this composite, however, the active structure is made of microscopic filaments. One individual filament is a hypha; in the plural, those fine fungal threads are called hyphae. The distinction matters because hyphae are fungal structures, not plant fibres in the substrate. Together, many hyphae form the mycelium that grows through the material.

responseBinding.questionText: As the threads spread, they form a binding ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: As the filaments extend, they branch around neighbouring particles and cross one another. Separate pieces that could once be poured begin to behave as one body. We can describe the connected arrangement as a binding network. The comparison with glue is only partial: a conventional adhesive is normally introduced as a liquid between surfaces, while here the connections develop as the organism spreads through the available spaces.

responseBinding.questionText: After forming, controlled ______ prevents continued fungal growth.

bindings.audiblePhrase: That growth must be brought to an end once the component has filled the intended form. Otherwise its dimensions and surface could continue to change during storage. The research review reports that controlled drying is commonly used to stop fungal growth on the substrate. This also lowers available water, but the effects should not be reversed: the evidence does not establish that only a separate high-temperature stage can end growth.

responseBinding.questionText: A thin ______ can protect the outer surface during brief liquid contact.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A bare composite may cushion an object well while remaining vulnerable to liquid at its outer surface. Designers can respond by applying a thin coating. Such a layer may reduce uptake during brief contact, but it does not make every design waterproof, and its chemistry may alter end-of-life options. The improvement must therefore be evaluated alongside disposal requirements rather than treated as an automatic environmental benefit.

responseBinding.questionText: Available plant matter → first ______ for the trial

bindings.audiblePhrase: First consider substrate selection. The review notes that agricultural wastes differ by type and are selected according to availability and suitability. For this teaching comparison, the incoming plant matter is therefore selected before further preparation; obviously unsuitable foreign pieces are excluded. Washing may remove surface dirt, but it does not decide which plant fraction enters the trial.

responseBinding.questionText: Larger pieces → ______ for more consistent size

bindings.audiblePhrase: The retained pieces then pass through a cutting mill and are shredded to make their size more consistent. They should not become fine powder, since densely packed dust would leave little air space. Controlled variation is the aim: fragments should mix evenly yet remain open enough for gases to move through the bed.

responseBinding.questionText: During incubation → growth and colonisation affected by ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Next comes incubation, when the fungus spreads through the prepared substrate. The review identifies pH as one condition that can affect both mycelial growth and colonisation. In a teaching comparison, technicians would therefore record this condition at regular intervals before the developing material moves to the shaping stage; particle size has already been set.

responseBinding.questionText: Colonised mixture → placed into ______ for shaping

bindings.audiblePhrase: After a fungal culture has been introduced and has begun to establish, the developing mixture must acquire the geometry of the package. It is placed into moulds that define corners, trays or protective blocks. A flat rack could support a piece later, but it would not impose the required three-dimensional form. At this stage the container is therefore also a shaping tool.

responseBinding.questionText: After direct liquid exposure → measure ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: After the shaped samples have been dried, the final stage is performance testing. One measurement is water absorption: researchers record how much liquid the composite takes up under a stated test condition. The review reports substantial variation between composites and identifies high uptake as an important limitation. This measure concerns direct contact with water; it does not justify a claim that ordinary changes in ambient humidity make a stored component expand or contract.
